newsitem.title: japan: TIFFE Euroyen mirrors slow cash market in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen mirrors slow cash market in Tokyo.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen futures contract ended Monday's session on TIFFE unchanged, mirroring a slow cash market, traders said.
The September was stuck in a narrow range of 99.23-25 and ended at 99.24, unchanged from the Friday's settlement.
The market is waiting for the U.S. Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday to see whether it gives a clue to direction.
The key three-month certificate of deposit (CD) was offered at 0.51 percent, unchanged since Thursday. Turnover in the key CD in the past few weeks has slowed to a trickle.
Some attributed a lack of turnover in the long end of the money market to a subtle change in market sentiment.

Shoji Kitta, managing director of Tokyo Tanshi Co Ltd, Japan's largest money broker, said: "The market expects a firming, though only a modest one, in the short-term rates in early next year without any official move by the central bank."
An expected firming will be due to chances of a slight change in the market's assessment of the economy, he added.
The market has been taking a more pessimistic, harsher view of the economy than the government.
But such pessimism may lessen if the government adopts a supplementary budget of around 5.5 trillion yen and changes its decision to discontinue income tax cuts, Kitta said.
The government will soon decide whether to continue the special income tax cuts, in place since last fiscal year, to boost the stalled economy, analysts said.
The new optimism towards the economy has been making investors reluctant to park cash in three-month CDs offering an extremely low yield, Kitta said.
The key overnight call rate, which was traded at 0.48-0.49 percent, is likely to firm to 0.51-0.52 percent towards the New Year to reflect year-end fund demand, traders said.
The weighted average of the key call rate was 0.46 percent.
